summary_paragraph: An elderly female with a history of chronic pain, recurrent venous thromboembolism on warfarin, and prior gastrointestinal bleeding presented with left elbow pain and was found to have severe anemia (hemoglobin 5.4 g/dL) and an elevated INR of 6.0. The anemia was attributed to a recurrent gastrointestinal bleed, likely exacerbated by anticoagulation and poor oral intake. She received vitamin K, two units of fresh frozen plasma, and four units of packed red blood cells, with improvement in hemoglobin to 28.5%. Her warfarin was held and later restarted at discharge after shared decision-making due to high thrombotic risk. She developed transient volume overload requiring IV furosemide but stabilized. Elbow pain resolved spontaneously, and imaging was unremarkable. She was discharged home with improved energy, instructions to monitor weight and INR, and follow-up for ongoing management of GI bleeding risk and anticoagulation.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic heart failure
Anticoagulants causing adverse effects in therapeutic use
Other persistent mental disorders due to conditions classified elsewhere
